name: Royal Pebble voice command grammar
status: Design reference for v1.1 Phase 5 (docs/DESIGN.md §11). Runtime: src/pkjs/voice.js (grammar) + src/pkjs/data/voice-HM.js (generated venue lexicon).
pipeline_summary: raw transcript -> normalise (sentences -> clauses) -> parse each clause into an intent with slot SPANS -> resolve spans (venue matcher, cabin table) -> merge clauses -> one result -> confirm screen (HEARD + FROM/TO or YOU'RE AT).

output_schema.intent: SET_LOCATION | ROUTE | ROUTE_COMBINED | CLOSEST_RESTROOM | LOCATION_REFUSED | OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN | INCOMPLETE | NO_MATCH
output_schema.A: start: venue span text, or a special token, or null (= current route start, 9.4)
output_schema.B: destination: venue span text, or a special token, or null
output_schema.cabin: the cabin number heard, digits only, or null (routing only, never stored beyond the current start)
output_schema.A_target: canonical venue name from venues.js (or directory place) after matching
output_schema.reason: LOCATION_REFUSED: restroom | elevator | stairs | deck | multi_spot; NO_MATCH: no_command | no_place | empty
output_schema.deck: a deck hint heard with a venue ("main dining room on deck 5"), or the deck of @deck:N

special_tokens.@mycabin: the stateroom set on the phone (Me tab). "my cabin", "my room", "our stateroom", "home"...
special_tokens.@cabin:NNNN: a spoken cabin number (4 digits on decks 3-9 and 17, 5 digits on decks 10-14 for HM)
special_tokens.@here: here / this place / where I am = the current route start; resolved to A = null
special_tokens.@restroom: any restroom synonym (26 restrooms, not a directory place)
special_tokens.@forelev / @aftelev: the named banks, directory places "Fore elevators" / "Aft elevators"
special_tokens.@deck:N: deck N (not a place; can qualify a venue or a cabin)

SET_LOCATION.what: Sets the spoken route start for 1.5 h (9.4). Only one-spot places: landmark venues, a cabin number, or my cabin (resets to the cabin).
patterns: {I_AM} in {CABIN}   (bare 4-5 digit number that is a real cabin)
at {A} | near {A} | in {CABIN_WORD} {CABIN}   ("I'm" dropped by ASR)
my location is {A} | set (my) location (to) {A} | start (from|at) {A} | routes start (at|from) {A}
guards: "I'm going/heading/walking to X", "I'm looking for X", "I'm on my way to X", "I'm trying to get to X" are ROUTE, not SET_LOCATION: the location pattern needs a PREP right after I_AM (plus optional ADVERB).
A location span that contains " to " ("I'm at the escape room to the Aqua Theater") becomes ROUTE_COMBINED.
A location span that is @restroom, @elevator, @forelev/@aftelev, @stairs or @deck:N is LOCATION_REFUSED.
"My cabin is 8924" / "set my cabin to 8924" is not a location: OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN topic stateroom (set it on the phone).

ROUTE.what: Route from A (or the current start) to B. Opens the confirm screen, then the Route screen (9.2).
patterns: {B} from {A}                        (bare, dropped words: "Windjammer from my room")
{A} {B}                             ("to" dropped: only when the span splits into two known venues)
where is|where's|where are {B}     (OWNER DECISION D1: recommended = ROUTE)

question_how: how do I get back to
question_distance: how long does it take to get to
imperative: show me how to get to
back_home: how do I get back to my room
how do I get back (bare: OWNER DECISION D6)

after_trigger_prepositions: for (only when no later "to"; "directions for the spa")
top_phrasings: How do I get to the Windjammer?
How do I get from the Solarium to my cabin?
guards: B = @restroom turns the route into CLOSEST_RESTROOM (from A).
A = @restroom/@elevator/@forelev/@aftelev/@stairs/@deck:N is LOCATION_REFUSED (only one-spot places can be a start).
B = @there, or nothing after the trigger, is INCOMPLETE.
An unresolved B whose words look like an event ("show", "trivia", "party"...) is OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN schedule ("where is <event>").
"head to X" is the verb (ROUTE); "the head" / "nearest head" is a restroom.

ROUTE_COMBINED.what: A location statement and a route question in one utterance: A = the stated location, B = the destination. Observed in the real test ("I'm at the escape room. How do I get to the Aqua Theater?").
patterns: {SET_LOCATION} (and|so) {ROUTE with no A}   (one sentence, no punctuation: the clause splitter cuts before the route trigger)
{I_AM} {PREP} {A}, {B}?   -> not combined (bare B after a location is too loose); see slot_rules
top_phrasings: I'm at the escape room. How do I get to the Aqua Theater?
I'm in cabin 8924, how do I get to the Solarium?
We're at Central Park and want to go to the Boardwalk
guards: If the ROUTE clause already has its own A, it wins and the location clause is ignored (confirm screen shows FROM).
Whether a combined utterance ALSO sets the spoken start (9.4) is OWNER DECISION D4 (recommended: yes).

CLOSEST_RESTROOM.what: Route to the closest restroom from A (or from the current start). Same page as Hold Select on a place page (9.2).
patterns: (where is|where's|how do I get to|take me to|I need) (the)? (closest|nearest)? {RESTROOM}
how do I get from {A} to (the)? {RESTROOM}

RESTROOM: the head / nearest head / closest head (not "head to")

guards: "from the restroom to X" and "I'm at the restroom" are LOCATION_REFUSED ("There are 26 restrooms").

LOCATION_REFUSED.what: A many-spot place was given as a location or route start. Design rule 9.6: "Only one-spot places can be a location".
triggers: ROUTE / CLOSEST_RESTROOM with A in that set
SET_LOCATION to a matched venue that has several separate spots (Running Track) -> reason multi_spot (matcher side; OWNER DECISION D8)
top_phrasings: From the bathroom to the Solarium

OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN.what: Recognised but not in Phase 5: answer "not yet" instead of NO_MATCH, so the guest learns it is planned.

schedule: where is <event> (unresolved span with event words)

OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN.event_words: see tables.event_words (only used when the span does not match a venue first)

INCOMPLETE.what: A command was recognised but its place is missing: "How do I get to", "Take me", "I'm at", "How do I get from the Solarium", "How do I get there".

NO_MATCH.what: Nothing recognised (no_command), a place that matched nothing (no_place), or an empty transcript (empty). Always show HEARD and a TRY example.

CLOSEST_BAR.what: Voice only (owner, 2026-09-28): the nearest bar, chosen by the route planner from the bars flagged B in the lexicon, the same way as the nearest restroom. From the current start, or from a place said in the same breath.
patterns: where is the bar | where's the bar
where can (I|we) (get|grab|find) a drink | drinks | a beer | a cocktail
I need a drink | I could use a beer | let's get a drink
{I_AM} at {A}. where can I get a drink?  (from A)
CLOSEST_BAR.notes: A named bar (Schooner Bar, Sand Bar) and "the pub" (Boot & Bonnet Pub, the only pub) stay ROUTE to that venue. "Wine bar" has two candidates and is left to the venue matcher. "I'm at the bar" is refused (many bars). Candidates exclude Casino Royale (the Casino filter exists for guests who avoid it), Crown Lounge and Suite Lounge (restricted), and coffee places. Opening hours aren't known offline, so the route screen can't say whether the bar is open.

CLOSEST_COFFEE.what: Voice only (owner, 2026-09-28): the nearest coffee place (flag C: Starbucks, Cafe Promenade, Park Cafe), found by the route planner like the nearest restroom. From the current start, or a place said in the same breath.
patterns: where can (I|we) (get|grab) a coffee | a latte | an espresso
I need coffee | I could use a cup of coffee
where can I get a latte from {A}
CLOSEST_COFFEE.notes: "Starbucks" said by name stays ROUTE to Starbucks. "I'm at the coffee shop" is refused (several places).

SNACK.what: Voice only (owner, 2026-09-28): a snack or a bite outside dining hours goes to Cafe Promenade, open 24 hours. Output is ROUTE (or ROUTE_COMBINED) with B_target Cafe Promenade and via: "snack", so the confirm screen can say it's open 24 hours.
patterns: where can I get a snack | something to eat | a bite to eat
I'm hungry | midnight snack | late night food
SNACK.notes: Named food places stay themselves ("pizza" = Sorrento's, "Cafe Promenade" without via). Dining-room requests go to the Me tab's Main dining room (1.4.8).

asr_artifacts.where: between two place spans or after a route trigger
asr_artifacts.rule: A lone "two/too/2" with words on both sides becomes "to", unless the word before is deck/room/level/floor/cabin/stateroom/number (then it is the digit). Inside a digit run, choose by cabin validity (see numbers).
asr_artifacts.risk: HIGH: "cabin 8924 two the Solarium" vs "cabin 89242". Resolved by trying both and keeping the reading where every number is a real cabin.

asr_artifacts.rule: Only when a later " to " exists in the same clause ("for the Solarium to the Windjammer"). Otherwise "for" means "to" ("directions for the spa").
asr_artifacts.risk: MEDIUM: "in front of" is a location preposition, handled before this rule.

asr_artifacts.rule: Canonicalise to the token "iam" before intent matching.
Cabin words followed by 3-5 digits become @cabin:N. Bare "cabin" without a number is @mycabin.
asr_artifacts.risk: MEDIUM: "Kevin" is also a name; only mapped before digits.

asr_artifacts.rule: Restroom synonyms are replaced BEFORE cabin synonyms so "rest room" is never read as "the room" (= my cabin).
asr_artifacts.risk: HIGH if the order is wrong.

heard: eight thousand nine hundred twenty four
asr_artifacts.rule: Number words -> digit groups, groups concatenated (spoken grouping is how people say room numbers), thousands separators and hyphens between digits removed.
"oh"/"o" is 0 only next to another number word; otherwise it is filler.
Concatenate; validity decides.
Keep it as @cabin:892; the resolver answers "Say all 4 or 5 digits".

heard: deck eight cabin nine twenty four
asr_artifacts.rule: deck N + cabin word + 3 digits (or 3 digits + on deck N) = N followed by the 3 digits, when that is a real cabin.
"to/too/for" between number words may be a digit (2/4). Keep the reading that gives a real cabin.

heard: eight nine two four to six nine oh two
asr_artifacts.rule: Joined reading 892426902 is not a cabin; split at "to".
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Venue matcher: compare with spaces removed; accept a unique prefix of 5+ letters; small edit distance on 7+ letters.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Space-free compare + theatre/theater spelling.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Spoken alias (Royal code royal-escape-room). Must win over the cabin rule for "room".
Only in "after elevators" / "aft elevator(s)". "after" elsewhere is left alone.
Rare; mapped only as a whole phrase.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Spoken alias. Also why "mass" is not an event word.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Spoken alias / compact compare.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Spoken alias.
Venue form: lives in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json (one source of truth). Apostrophes are dropped before compare; edit distance covers one letter.
Lowercase; split on . ? ! ; into sentences; commas are soft (removed).

heard: How do I get to the how do I get to the Solarium
asr_artifacts.rule: The clause splitter cuts at every strong trigger; an INCOMPLETE clause is dropped when a later clause is complete.

heard: the wind jam are two cabin
asr_artifacts.rule: Too far gone: NO_MATCH with TRY (this is the mocked WatchVoiceNoMatch case).

normalisation.name: keep raw
normalisation.does: Keep the transcript exactly as returned for the HEARD line.
normalisation.rationale: The guest must see what the phone heard (9.6).

normalisation.name: unicode and case
normalisation.does: Curly quotes -> straight, é -> e, lowercase.

normalisation.name: digit punctuation
normalisation.rationale: Do this before stripping punctuation or "8,924" becomes two numbers.

normalisation.name: sentence split
normalisation.does: Split on . ? ! ; : and ellipsis. Commas are removed (soft).
normalisation.rationale: Observed transcripts come back as several sentences; the combined intent depends on it.
normalisation.pitfalls: A pause can split "Boardwalk. To the Solarium." -> merged by slot_rules.

normalisation.name: strip punctuation and apostrophes
normalisation.does: Drop apostrophes ("i'm" -> "im", "sorrento's" -> "sorrentos"), other punctuation -> space, collapse spaces.

normalisation.name: contractions and I-am
normalisation.does: im / i am / i m / we are / aim (start) / am (start) / were (start) -> "iam"; "iam add" -> "iam at"; wheres -> where is; whats -> what is; howd -> how do; wanna -> want to; gotta -> have to; lets -> let us.
normalisation.pitfalls: "were" and "am" only at the start of a sentence.

normalisation.name: numbers
normalisation.does: Number words -> digit groups -> concatenated; choose between "to/too/two/for" as digit or word by cabin validity; "oh" is zero only next to another number.
normalisation.rationale: Must run before filler removal ("oh" is also a filler) and before the to/two fix.
normalisation.pitfalls: Never turn "to" into 2 outside a digit run. "Main Dining Room 5", "150 Central Park", "deck 5" are numbers but not cabins.

normalisation.name: correction split
normalisation.does: Split at no / sorry / i mean / actually / wait / scratch that / make that when not at the start; the right part is flagged as a correction.
normalisation.pitfalls: "no" at the start is just filler.

normalisation.name: filler removal
normalisation.does: Remove um, uh, hey, hi, ok, so, well, please, thanks, pebble, hey pebble, excuse me, can you (tell me), could you, do you know, tell me, I want to know, I was wondering, just, help me, on the ship, on board.
normalisation.pitfalls: Whole words only: venue names like "Play", "Focus", "Fuel", "Loyalty" must not be touched. "like" is NOT a filler here.

normalisation.name: place-class synonyms (order matters)
normalisation.does: 1 restroom words -> @restroom; 2 fore/aft elevators -> @forelev/@aftelev, other elevator words -> @elevator; 3 stairs words -> @stairs; 4 cabin word + number (and deck N cabin NNN) -> @cabin:N, bare real 4-5 digit cabin -> @cabin:N; 5 deck N -> @deck:N; 6 my cabin / my room / home / bare cabin -> @mycabin; 7 here / this place / where I am -> @here.
normalisation.rationale: Restrooms before cabins ("rest room"), numbered cabins before @mycabin, "escape room"/"living room"/"card room"/"dining room" are never @mycabin because only "my/our/the room" is.

normalisation.name: command-word ASR fixes
normalisation.does: Lone too/two/2 between words -> to (see asr_artifacts). for/front/form -> from inside route clauses only.

normalisation.name: clause split
normalisation.does: Cut a sentence before a strong trigger that is not at its start (how do, where is, take me, iam at, closest, what is next, ...), optionally preceded by and/so/but/then; not when the previous word is "iam"/"i" or "the".
normalisation.rationale: Handles "I'm at the escape room how do I get to the Aqua Theater" with no punctuation, and stutters.

normalisation.name: slot cleanup
normalisation.does: Per span: strip leading the/a/an/that/closest/nearest, trailing please/located/is/on/at/from here (-> A=@here); trailing "on deck N" becomes a deck hint.

slot_rules.detail: Priority inside a route clause: "from A to B" > "to B from A" > "B from A" > "A to B" > "to B" > "B". Split at the FIRST " to " (no HM venue name contains the word "to"). Location prepositions "next to" / "close to" are consumed before splitting.
When a single span does not match any venue, try every split point: if both halves match venues, A = left, B = right ("Boardwalk the Solarium").

Parse each clause, then merge: a SET_LOCATION plus a ROUTE (or CLOSEST_RESTROOM) without A -> ROUTE_COMBINED (or CLOSEST_RESTROOM from that place). Otherwise the LAST complete in-scope clause wins; INCOMPLETE and NO_MATCH clauses are dropped when another clause is complete ("Thanks." "Hello.").
A clause that is only a place followed by a route clause without A ("Boardwalk." "To the Solarium.") -> A = that place.
A correction clause that is a full command replaces the previous result; a bare place replaces the previous result's last slot (B for routes, A for locations, A for restrooms).
"I'm at X. How do I get from Y to Z?": the explicit route start Y wins; X is not used. The confirm screen shows FROM Y.
"I'm at X. I'm at Y." or "I'm at X, I mean Y": the last one wins.

"from X to Y to Z": A = X, B = everything after the first "to"; that span will not match and the dropped-"to" split may pick Y+Z. Result shown on confirm; via-points are not supported. Recommend NO_MATCH-style TRY if unresolved.
Trigger with nothing after it, or "from A" only, or B = there -> INCOMPLETE with a TRY example.
@here as A = the current start (A = null). "closest restroom to me" = from the current start. @here as a location ("I'm here") -> INCOMPLETE.
@mycabin as A or B; if no stateroom is set on the phone, answer "Add your stateroom on the phone" (existing wording). As a location it resets the spoken start to the cabin.
Any @cabin:N fills `cabin`. Not a real cabin -> "No cabin N on Harmony". Fewer than 4 digits -> "Say all 4 or 5 digits". Never stored beyond the current start.
"deck 5" alone is @deck:5: refused as a location, and as a destination it is OWNER DECISION D5. "on deck N" after a venue is a hint (Main Dining Room 5, elevator lobby).
Venue matcher fails -> event words? OUT_OF_SCOPE_KNOWN schedule : NO_MATCH no_place, keeping the spans for the HEARD line.
"dining room", "theater", "pool": spoken aliases map them to a default or to a family (Main Dining Room 3|4|5 -> the floor nearest the start). OWNER DECISION D3.
Perfect Day at CocoCay etc: "CocoCay is ashore" (no GPS lines ashore, 9.1).

responses._layout: Voice screens use the directory gray bar labelled `Ask` (confirm, errors) or `Route` (results). HEARD shows the raw transcript in quotes. Keep each line under ~20 characters at Gothic 18, ~26 at Gothic 14. Select confirms, Hold Select asks again.

tables._moved: The runtime grammar tables live in src/pkjs/voice.js (GRAMMAR), hand-edited and covered by test/pkjs/voice.test.js. Venue names, aliases and their mishearings live only in tools/voice/venue-mishearings-HM.json. Multi-spot and ashore flags are fields there (location: false) or come from venues.js (Ashore).
